crs_note: UTM Zone 16N, NAD83, metres. All georeferencing and footprint data lands here first; scene coordinates are local East-North-Up metres from the origin below.
note: The centre of the Chicago River forks at Wolf Point — the junction of the North Branch, South Branch and main stem — as drawn on the Wright 1834 survey, independently georeferenced for this project. Derived 2026-08-09; full memo in docs/RESEARCH/datum_derivation.md; re-derivable from the committed traces with tools/rederive_datum.py.

derivation.method: Eight ground-control points were placed by hand on the Wright 1834 scan at surviving street intersections (including the State & Madison PLSS section corner) and matched to modern OpenStreetMap intersection nodes; a least-squares affine transform from pixel space to EPSG:26916 was fitted with RMS 17.5 m (max 32.7 m, at a visibly warped region of the sheet). The forks junction pixel was read from the map and transformed. The Hathaway 1834 LOC scan was independently georeferenced the same way (five GCPs, RMS 17.7 m) as a cross-check.

cross_checks.note: Three witnesses: the Wright-derived point (adopted), the independently georeferenced Hathaway forks 57.9 m NE of it, and the modern OSM river-junction node 39.4 m south of it. The Wright point sits between them, and the junction has not physically moved since 1834 — the banks were wharfed, the Y stayed. The brief's placeholder origin (41.8885, -87.6385) was 203 m NNW of the derived point, up the North Branch.

derivation.control: Modern control from OpenStreetMap intersection nodes (Overpass API, fetched 2026-08-09; multi-node crossings averaged, max spread 6.4 m). Warped to street intersections whose centerlines survive unchanged, anchored by the State & Madison section corner. Buildings were not used as control — the buildings are what this datum exists to locate.
derivation.residual_note: Both 1834 sheets carry real anisotropic paper stretch (Wright 3.7%, Hathaway 4.5% axis-scale difference), so a global affine cannot do better than tens of metres locally. Treat ~20 m as the working horizontal uncertainty of any position traced from these maps, and the ~58 m cross-map disagreement as the honest ceiling.

vertical.internal: Z = 0.0 ft at the summer-1835 lake and river water surface
vertical.export_note: ASL = Z + 580.0. Do not mix Chicago City Datum (1847 low-water mark, on the obsolete mean-tide-New-York reference) with NAVD88 figures; the discrepancy is most of a foot in a landscape whose entire natural relief is under fifteen feet. See docs/EPOCHS.md.
vertical.lake_stage_note: No 1835 Lake Michigan stage record located. The mid-1830s fall in a high-water phase; 580 +/- 1.5 ft ASL is the working assumption. Check NOAA/GLERL historical Michigan-Huron reconstructions to narrow it.

units.historical_note: Period surveys are in feet, chains and links. Convert at ingest and record the original figure in the attribute note. Do not carry mixed units into the dataset.
